review_findings: The new qwen2-action-json-v1 profile is explicit; existing generic GPT-2/Qwen consumers and the strict action parser are unchanged. No automatic fallback is added.

Pinned XGrammar 0.2.7 and apache-tvm-ffi 0.1.12 derive syntax only from exact advertised public tool schemas and the existing final-claim shape. Tool/action choice, arguments, values, citations and whether to finish remain model-owned. Empty or semantically wrong finals remain possible.

Generation uses declared structural key order without changing which legal action/value can be represented. Parser-only uniqueness, UTF-8/byte limits and complete-action validation remain authoritative. No corpus, memory state, expected answer or verifier result enters grammar construction.

Complete detached request bytes are bound to each authenticated artifact and checked against its request digest at execution. No hidden schema message or expected answer changes the recorded input. A/B/A and repeated artifacts retain their own advertised tool grammar.

At most 64 request bindings exist per consumer lifetime. Capacity failure is explicit, no binding is silently evicted, and close clears the state. Fresh compiler/matcher and request-local model KV state are used per execution.

Runtime identity binds the base model runtime, exact grammar versions, schema digest, compiler/ordering/whitespace policy, termination and special-token settings, capacity and no-repair policy. Grammar version or policy drift rejects dispatch.

The CPU float32 mask wrapper checks initial and extended prefixes, every selected token including the last, legal tokenizer membership, finite logits, valid mask layout, remaining output bound and nonempty choices. Mask and membership allocations are explicitly CPU even under a different default device.

Raw generated IDs and costs are preserved. No token is appended or output repaired. An incomplete prefix at the reservation reaches the unchanged parser and fails with known cost; a complete valid action ending exactly at the bound need not invent EOS.

The checker independently replays tokenization, constrained identity, request-specific grammar, strict actions, causal links, verifiers and accounting. It explicitly does not authenticate execution or reconstruct unrecorded logits.

The shared policy clarification describes obtaining requested records, revising unchanged repeated retrieval and completing explicitly requested lifecycle actions before claiming completion. It supplies no fixed action sequence, top_k, fixture fact, expected value or forced write. Any next campaign changes both grammar and policy, so causality cannot be attributed to grammar alone.

Optional packaging and docs retain exact CPU runtime admission and the two-stage CPU Torch then agent-action installation. Linux x86_64 Triton is a transitive packaging surface, not a claimed GPU execution path. Cross-platform optional-profile qualification remains unclaimed.
